text: A contravariant functor F: C → D acts on a morphism f: A → B by producing:
choices: a morphism F(f): F(A) → F(B) with F(g∘f) = F(g)∘F(f)
a morphism F(f): F(B) → F(A) with F(g∘f) = F(f)∘F(g)
a natural transformation between two functors
explanation: A contravariant functor reverses arrows: f: A → B is sent to F(f): F(B) → F(A), and composition order flips, F(g∘f) = F(f)∘F(g) — equivalently it is a covariant functor on C^op. Option A is the covariant law; the paradigm contravariant functor is Hom(−, A), acting by precomposition.
